title: Design of a minimal, allosteric, and ATPase-like machine using mechanical linkages
note: Points were consolidated by hand from the three public reviews. 'reviewers' records which of the three raised each point, so consensus points (>=2) can be weighted separately from single-reviewer points. Only substantive critiques are listed; praise is excluded.

points.point: The manuscript is very dense and hard to follow; the notation and microstate labels (e.g. {S/L}:{10,5}) obscure the central ideas. A simpler schematic, a mapping of state labels, and a step-by-step worked example of a productive cycle are needed; the supplementary videos need more explanation.

The framework fits mechanically gated motor proteins but may not generalize to allosteric enzymes that work through conformational ensembles, dynamic coupling, or entropy-driven regulation; the scope should be discussed more carefully.
The reported behaviour depends on finely tuned parameter choices and rate hierarchies; a broader sensitivity/robustness analysis over the parameter space is needed.
Treating states as binary rigid-or-flexible oversimplifies the continuous energy landscapes and thermal fluctuations of real biomolecules; the limitation should be discussed.

The nonequilibrium thermodynamics is underdeveloped: the relation to ATP chemical potential, free-energy dissipation, entropy production, and the energetic cost of futile cycles should be made explicit.

With hundreds of microstates enumerated it is unclear which states and pathways dominate the dynamics; a coarse-grained analysis of the key states and transitions would improve interpretability and comparison with experiment.

The energetic constraints are not derived from physical principles: the kinetic rates, binding constants, and reactivity mechanisms are imposed rather than following from interaction energies under thermal fluctuations.

The logic of the derivation should be clarified up front: which are the fundamental hypotheses, which results are derived from them, and which need additional assumptions. The model mixes physical assumptions that yield kinetic features with global kinetic assumptions that yield microscopic features.

Rather than generalizing to more elaborate models, the opposite may be desirable: could the main results, e.g. the trade-offs defining an optimal cleavage rate, be obtained from an even simpler model?

The modelled cycle is not faithful to the ATPase it is inspired by: real allosteric regulation does not require the ligand to displace both products; one product (P) dissociates spontaneously while the larger one (ADP) is allosterically displaced.
No comparison is made with chemical rates actually measured for the motivating biological systems; such a comparison would be instructive.

Despite being framed as a mechanical model, the mechanical aspects only serve to restrict allowed transitions and are abstracted away in the simulations; physical degrees of freedom are never simulated, so it is not actually a mechanical model.
